article_title: From Cognitive Outsourcing to Reallocation: A 3P Analysis of Student–Generative AI Engagement in Unsupervised Assessments
citation: Yan, W., Cui, Y., Chiu, T. K. F., Nakajima, T., & Kozima, H. (2026). From cognitive outsourcing to reallocation: A 3P analysis of student–generative AI engagement in unsupervised assessments. Australasian Journal of Educational Technology, 42(3), 41–61. https://doi.org/10.14742/ajet.11725
title: The 3P (presage-process-product) model operationalised for GenAI-supported assessment
description: The study applies Biggs' presage-process-product model to student–generative AI engagement in unsupervised higher-education assessments. It "operationalised and contextualised the 3P model in GenAI-supported assessment by articulating how presage factors shape distinct process patterns and perceived outcomes." Presage factors (intentions, contexts) are linked to process patterns of GenAI use and to perceived product outcomes, providing an explanatory framework for analysing human–GenAI collaboration in assessment.
requirements: Analysis requires data on students' GenAI usage intentions, dialogue patterns and integration with other learning activities in authentic assessment contexts
constraints: Developed and illustrated through qualitative analysis of undergraduates in Japan and China in after-class assessment contexts
target_learning_goals: cognitive engagement with generative AI in assessment tasks
examples: The study analysed 38 undergraduate students from Japan and China, examining their GenAI usage intentions, dialogue patterns and integration with other learning activities.
key_sources: Yan, W., Cui, Y., Chiu, T. K. F., Nakajima, T., & Kozima, H. (2026). article_title: NRF2011-EDU001-EL001 EduLab Project Scaling-up Reflections on Using Open Source Physics
citation: Wee, Loo Kang, Lim, Ai Phing, & Lye, Sze Yee. (2014). Scaling-up Reflections on Using Open Source Physics. https://weelookang.blogspot.sg/2013/03/moe-excel-fest-2013-scaling.html
title: 3Ps Scaling-Up Framework: Product, Process and People with Dimensions of Scaling Up
description: The article organises its scaling-up lessons using a framework of Product, Process and People, presented in Figure 1 as the "3Ps Scaling–Up Framework, Product, Process and People with Dimensions of Scaling Up in brackets (Dede, 2007)". Product covers the Easy Java Simulation–Open Source Physics toolkit, ease of download at "zero dollars", and evolving JavaScript models; Process covers creative commons licenses, alignment to learning practices as a virtual lab, and MOE-NIE eduLab support; People covers experts, passionate teachers and student advocates. The article uses it to explain how models moved from researchers to teachers in RVHS, YJC, IJC, AJC and SRJC.
requirements: Requires collaboration among experts, passionate teachers and supporting specialist divisions
constraints: Applied to scaling open-source physics computer models in Singapore schools under eduLab funding
target_learners: Junior college physics students in Singapore
target_learning_goals: Physics inquiry learning through interactive computer models
examples: The project's models and lesson packages were shared with teachers across RVHS, YJC, IJC, AJC and SRJC with worksheets and resources
key_sources: Wee, Loo Kang, Lim, Ai Phing, & Lye, Sze Yee. (2014). Scaling-up Reflections on Using Open Source Physics. https://weelookang.blogspot.sg/2013/03/moe-excel-fest-2013-scaling.html

article_title: Transforming the Preparation of Physics GTAs: Curriculum Development
citation: Emily Alicea-Muñoz, Carol Subiño Sullivan, and Michael F. Schatz. (2021). Transforming the Preparation of Physics GTAs: Curriculum Development. https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.00168
title: 3P Framework: full integration of Pedagogy, Physics, and Professional Development for GTA preparation
description: The 3P Framework is the organizing model the article develops for comprehensive GTA preparation. It posits that a program must fully integrate pedagogical knowledge, physics content, and professional development, visualized as a Venn diagram whose intersections matter as much as the circles. The article states that there must be full integration between pedagogical knowledge, physics content, and professional development strategies, because pedagogy alone, physics alone, or professional development alone is insufficient for novice physics instructors. The Pedagogy-Physics intersection is grounded in the Pedagogical Content Knowledge framework.
requirements: Full integration of all three themes; each P alone is stated to be insufficient for a useful and valuable program
Instructor capacity to map course topics onto the three themes and act on the gaps revealed
constraints: Developed for first-time GTAs teaching introductory physics labs and recitations at an R1 institution; the authors propose it can be applied to other institutional or disciplinary contexts
target_learners: first-year Ph.D. students serving as first-time graduate teaching assistants in physics
target_learning_goals: explaining physics concepts and addressing preconceptions
giving and receiving feedback on teaching
examples: The authors mapped the Fall 2013 pilot course contents and the Fall 2019 course onto the 3P Framework's Venn diagram, with gaps in the early version filled by Fall 2019
key_sources: Emily Alicea-Muñoz, Carol Subiño Sullivan, and Michael F. Schatz. (2021). Transforming the Preparation of Physics GTAs: Curriculum Development. https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.00168

article_title: Utilizing Optic Fiber Interferometry in Forced Vibration Experimentation for Educational Purposes
citation: Wang M, Zhou M, Ji H, Lan T. (2024). Utilizing Optic Fiber Interferometry in Forced Vibration Experimentation for Educational Purposes. https://doi.org/XXXX/XXXX
title: '3+2' segmented teaching model: 3 hours of guided experiments plus 2 hours of open exploration
description: The article proposes a modular lab-session structure in which students first complete guided experiments and then pursue open exploration. As printed, the "modular “3+2” teaching design (3 hours of guided experiments + 2 hours of open exploration) accommodates diverse learners", letting undergraduates focus on foundational principles while graduate students tackle advanced signal processing tasks. It is used to structure the OFI forced-vibration module and is offered as a scalable case study bridging classical theory with modern optical techniques.
requirements: Students receive prior basic training in interferometric diagnostics before the guided segment
target_learning_goals: experimental design and data analysis in precision measurement
examples: The OFI forced-vibration module was delivered under this structure, with guided alignment and quadrature-signal analysis followed by open exploration in which graduate students handled advanced signal processing tasks.
key_sources: Wang M, Zhou M, Ji H, Lan T. (2024). Utilizing Optic Fiber Interferometry in Forced Vibration Experimentation for Educational Purposes. https://doi.org/XXXX/XXXX

article_title: Insights from Educators on Building a More Cohesive Quantum Information Science and Engineering Education Ecosystem
citation: El-Adawy, S., Piña, A. R., Zwickl, B. M., & Lewandowski, H. J. (2025). Insights from Educators on Building a More Cohesive Quantum Information Science and Engineering Education Ecosystem. arXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.01578
title: 3P-6Cs curriculum framework adapted for QISE education
description: The article adapts the 3P-6Cs framework of Khanna et al., which conceptualizes an educational program as "a complex adaptive system" through which students navigate to become professionals. It structures programs into three interconnected levels — Personal, Program, and Practice — and operationalizes six Program-level components for QISE: goals, curriculum, collaboration, collection, evaluation, and connections. The authors apply it with a SWOT lens to organize interview findings about QISE course and program development, focusing this study on the Program level.
requirements: A structured framework is needed because QISE, as a new and rapidly evolving field, lacks structured ways to address the many factors shaping education in the field.
constraints: The study focuses only on the Program level; the Personal and Practice levels are left for future research.
The framework alone does not capture challenges and opportunities, so it was combined with a SWOT analysis.
target_learners: undergraduate and graduate students in QISE courses and programs
target_learning_goals: preparing students for the quantum workforce through coherent QISE course and program design
examples: The authors coded 247 interview excerpts with the operationalized framework components and SWOT codes, then derived community-level themes for QISE courses and programs.
key_sources: El-Adawy, S., Piña, A. R., Zwickl, B. M., & Lewandowski, H. J. (2025). Insights from Educators on Building a More Cohesive Quantum Information Science and Engineering Education Ecosystem. arXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.01578
